chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from Safwan from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"When you accept land for cultivation (muzara'ah) with gold or silver, do not accept it for more than what you accepted it for; and if you accepted it for half or a third, you may accept it for more than what you accepted it for, because gold and silver are guaranteed (liable for loss)."

key_terms.تَقَبَّلْتَ: You accepted (in the context of entering a contract)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference in sharecropping rules when the capital is gold/silver versus a share of the crop?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between capital provided as currency (gold/silver) versus in-kind (crops) in Muzara'ah contracts, emphasizing that precious metals are 'guaranteed' (daman) against loss, thus capping the landlord's return at the initial principal. In contrast, in-kind capital involves risk-sharing, allowing the landlord to claim a larger portion if the harvest exceeds expectations. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle that the nature of the capital determines the liability structure, ensuring fairness when one party's contribution is fixed in value while the other's is subject to agricultural uncertainty.
